## Functions

### `async createRealmLifecycleGenerationHeadStorage(options)`

Reserve strictly increasing generations for one captured account and app. The account service root and hashed app path survive source reconstruction; the counter never resets when the operator's transient generation changes. Construction and readCurrent({ signal }) never initialize or allocate. allocateNext({ expected, signal }) requires exact observed absence (null) or the frozen { lifecycleGeneration, exactStorageSha256 } predecessor. Every successful reservation writes the next positive uint64 head. Callers cannot choose its value. Exhaustion fails closed; there is no reset or delete API. A dispatched-but-unconfirmed allocation may consume a generation. Recover with a fresh read and allocate a NEW value; a read is never an allocation receipt and must never be used to issue the observed reserved generation. This kernel-only source assumes cooperative protected OPFS writers. It is not lifecyclePort: a reserved high-water mark proves neither currentness nor retirement and creates no handle, participant, process owner, or intent. The future owner still needs exact post-switch teardown authority, live invalidation, authenticated acquisition, and protected-backend isolation. View branding and import confinement do not isolate hostile same-origin native storage access. No provider or application authority is activated.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
